Vital signs within normal limits.
Family meeting scheduled for 1400.

items.rationale: New self-injury with a stated function of relieving emotional numbness, a threat of a more lethal attempt tied to discharge, and splitting statements that idealize one nurse and devalue others are the findings the oncoming nurse must address: a safety assessment, removal of items usable for self-harm, and a consistent team response to the splitting. Group attendance, sleep, the declined phone call and the scheduled meeting are routine handoff information.

items.stem: Click to highlight the findings in the school nurse's note that suggest the student may have an eating disorder and warrant further assessment.

highlightSegments.text: 14-year-old student sent to the health office after nearly fainting in gym class.
Student wears an oversized sweatshirt although the classroom is warm and says she is 'always cold.'
Weight today is 5 kg lower than at the fall screening 4 months ago.
Teacher reports the student asks to go to the library during lunch most days.
Student reports she has been 'eating healthy' and cut out 'all the bad foods.'
No history of asthma or heart problems.
Pulse 54/min after resting for 10 minutes.
Student is on the honor roll and plays the violin.
Parent contacted and will pick the student up.
Student asks the nurse not to 'make a big deal of it.'

items.rationale: Near-syncope, marked weight loss, cold intolerance hidden under bulky clothing, avoiding the lunch period, rigid 'healthy' eating rules and resting bradycardia together form a pattern strongly suggestive of an eating disorder in an adolescent, and the nurse refers the student and family for medical and psychological assessment. High achievement is a common trait rather than a diagnostic finding, and the absence of cardiac history, the parent pickup and the request for privacy do not change the concern.

items.stem: Click to highlight the findings in the home visit note, 14 months after the death of the client's spouse, that suggest prolonged grief disorder and the need for referral.

highlightSegments.text: Home visit with an 80-year-old client whose spouse of 55 years died 14 months ago.
Client keeps a framed wedding photograph on the table and speaks warmly about the spouse.
Sets a place at the table for the spouse at every meal and says, 'I can't accept that he's gone.'
Has stopped attending church and the weekly card game, and has not seen friends in 6 months.
States, 'Life has no meaning now; I'm just waiting to join him.'
Has lost 6 kg since the funeral and sleeps in the recliner because 'the bed is too empty.'
Client's daughter calls every evening.
Takes medications correctly and the home is clean.
Attended a grief support group twice last spring.
Cried briefly when describing the funeral.

items.rationale: More than a year after the death, persistent inability to accept the loss with rituals that deny it, withdrawal from all social and spiritual activity, loss of meaning with a passive wish to die, and ongoing weight loss and disturbed sleep fit prolonged grief disorder with suicide risk and warrant referral for grief-focused therapy and a suicide risk assessment. Keeping photographs, speaking warmly about the spouse and brief tears are normal continuing bonds, and adherence, a clean home and a daughter's calls are protective.

items.stem: Click to highlight the findings in the outpatient note that indicate the client's post-traumatic stress disorder is improving after 12 weeks of trauma-focused therapy.

highlightSegments.text: Follow-up for a 38-year-old client with PTSD after a serious motor vehicle crash 1 year ago.
At intake: nightmares nightly, unable to ride in a car, missed 3 months of work.
Reports nightmares about once a week now.
Rode as a passenger to today's appointment on the highway where the crash occurred.
Returned to work full time 3 weeks ago.
Still avoids driving at night.
States, 'When I get the flashback feeling I use the grounding steps and it passes in a minute or two.'
Continues sertraline 100 mg daily; no side effects reported.
Partner attended the session.
Next appointment in 4 weeks.

items.rationale: A drop in nightmares from nightly to weekly, confronting the previously avoided highway, returning to full-time work, and using grounding skills to manage intrusive symptoms show reductions in re-experiencing, avoidance and functional impairment, the core targets of trauma-focused therapy. Remaining avoidance of night driving is an unmet goal, and the intake history, medication and follow-up interval are context rather than evidence of improvement.

items.stem: The nurse reviews the trended GAD-7 anxiety screening results for a client treated with escitalopram and weekly cognitive behavioral therapy. Which conclusion should the nurse draw?
options: The client should stop the medication because the score is now below 10
The client still has severe anxiety because the score is above 5
The combined treatment is effective and the client's anxiety has decreased from severe to mild
The slow initial change means the medication is not working and should be replaced
items.rationale: A GAD-7 falling from 19 (severe) to 6 (mild) with panic episodes eliminated, sleep restored and no missed work demonstrates a robust response to combined SSRI and cognitive behavioral therapy. SSRIs take 4 to 6 weeks for full effect, so modest early change is expected rather than failure, and treatment usually continues for months after remission to prevent relapse; a score of 5 to 9 is mild, not severe, anxiety.

items.stem: The nurse on a memory care unit reviews the trended data for a resident with dementia after starting a non-pharmacological plan for late-afternoon agitation. Which conclusion should the nurse draw?
options: The structured daytime activity and shortened nap are reducing sundowning and should be continued
The longer night sleep indicates oversedation
The exit-seeking stopped because the resident is becoming withdrawn and depressed
The resident needs a scheduled antipsychotic because agitation persisted on day 3
items.rationale: Replacing a long afternoon nap with daytime activity and outdoor light strengthened the resident's sleep-wake cycle, and the falling evening agitation, elimination of exit-seeking and consolidated 7-hour night sleep show the non-drug plan is working. Antipsychotics carry a boxed warning in dementia and are reserved for dangerous behavior that fails other measures; 7 hours of night sleep is normal rather than oversedation, and there is no evidence of depression.

items.stem: The community mental health nurse reviews the trended data for a client with schizophrenia who receives a monthly long-acting injectable antipsychotic. Which action should the nurse take first?
options: Document the findings and reassess at the July visit
Advise the client to increase sleep by going to bed earlier
Assess the content of the voices and the client's safety, and arrange an urgent provider visit to give the missed injection
Praise the client for attending one group and encourage more
trendRows: Same clothes as last visit, unwashed hair
items.rationale: A missed long-acting injection followed by rising hallucinations, falling sleep, withdrawal from groups and declining self-care is the early relapse signature in schizophrenia; because the voices are now 'telling me things,' the nurse first assesses for command content and safety and gets the medication restarted urgently. Waiting a month allows full decompensation, and praise or sleep hygiene advice do not address the missed antipsychotic or the safety risk.

items.stem: The nurse reviews the trended daily suicide risk screening for a client admitted with depression. Which conclusion should the nurse draw?
options: The client is testing staff and should be reminded of unit rules
Risk is unchanged because the client has had suicidal thoughts every day
Risk has escalated to a plan with preparatory behavior and the client requires immediate 1:1 continuous observation and removal of the item
Observation can be reduced because the client is disclosing thoughts openly
trendRows: 'I could use the cord from my hoodie'
Hoodie found tied to the bathroom rail
items.rationale: Movement from ideation without a plan to a specific method and a rehearsal or preparatory act is a marked escalation in imminent risk; 15-minute checks leave enough time to complete a hanging, so the client needs continuous 1:1 observation, removal of the cord and all similar items, and provider notification. Daily ideation is not 'unchanged' when a plan and behavior appear, labeling the act as testing dismisses a lethal cue, and disclosure does not lower risk.

items.stem: A client with schizophrenia insists that the nurse is an agent sent to poison the unit's water supply. For each nurse response, click to specify whether it is therapeutic or nontherapeutic.
matrixRows: 'I understand you feel frightened. I am a nurse here and the water is safe; would you like a sealed bottle?'
'That's ridiculous; why would I want to poison anyone?'
'Tell me more about how the agents contacted you, so I can understand the plan.'
'I can see this is very real to you, but I do not share that belief.'
'Let's go to the dayroom; the art group is starting in 5 minutes.'
'If you keep saying that, you will lose your phone privileges.'
items.rationale: With delusions the nurse acknowledges the client's feelings, presents reality briefly without arguing, and redirects to concrete activities; offering a sealed bottle meets the safety need without validating the belief. Arguing or ridiculing increases defensiveness and mistrust, exploring the delusion's details reinforces it, and threats punish a symptom the client cannot control.

items.stem: A nurse in a long-term care facility reviews findings about several residents. For each finding, click to specify whether it most suggests physical abuse, neglect, or financial exploitation.
matrixRows: Circular burns on the forearm that the resident says came from 'the heater'
Stage 3 pressure injury on the sacrum and a strong odor of urine at the morning assessment
A nephew who recently became power of attorney has stopped paying the facility bill, and the resident's watch and rings are missing
Resident has lost 6 kg in 2 months and the meal tray is routinely removed untouched without assistance
Resident signs over the monthly pension check to an aide who 'helps with shopping' but brings nothing back
Wrist bruising in a grip pattern and the resident says, 'They squeeze me when I'm slow'
items.rationale: Patterned burns and grip-mark bruises with a disclosure of rough handling indicate physical abuse; an unrelieved pressure injury, untreated incontinence and weight loss from meals removed without feeding assistance indicate neglect of basic care; and missing valuables, an unpaid bill after a change in power of attorney, and pension checks signed over without return are financial exploitation. All three are reportable to adult protective services or the long-term care ombudsman.

items.stem: A nurse in a pediatric clinic suspects that a 6-year-old child is being physically abused at home. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.
options: Report the suspicion to child protective services as required by law
Wait until the next visit to see whether new injuries appear before reporting
Confront the parent with the suspicion and ask for a confession
Promise the child that the nurse will keep everything a secret
Document the child's statements in the child's own words and describe injuries objectively
Interview the child separately from the caregiver using open-ended, non-leading questions
Photograph injuries according to facility policy with appropriate consent
items.rationale: Nurses are mandated reporters and must report reasonable suspicion promptly; objective documentation, verbatim quotes, a separate non-leading interview and policy-based photographs create the record that protects the child. Confronting the parent can escalate danger and is the investigator's role, delaying the report leaves the child at risk, and promising secrecy is a promise the nurse cannot keep and undermines trust when the report is made.

items.stem: The hospice nurse cares for a client in the final days of life and the client's family at home. Which interventions support the psychosocial needs of the client and family? Select all that apply.
options: Tell the family to stay in the room continuously so they do not miss the moment of death
Provide information about bereavement follow-up available after the death
Discourage the family from crying in front of the client to keep the atmosphere calm
Explain the expected physical changes of dying so the family is not frightened by them
Encourage family members to talk to the client and say what they need to say, even if the client appears unresponsive
Ask about spiritual or cultural practices the family wants observed at the time of death
items.rationale: Hearing is thought to persist near death, so encouraging family communication, honoring spiritual and cultural rituals, preparing the family for changes such as irregular breathing and mottling, and offering bereavement resources address the psychosocial needs of both client and family. Insisting on continuous presence creates guilt and exhaustion, and suppressing tears denies the natural expression of grief.

items.stem: A client with schizophrenia says to the nurse, 'Can't you hear them? They are laughing at me from the ceiling.' Which response by the nurse is most therapeutic?
options: 'I do not hear any voices, but I can see that you are upset. Let's walk to the dayroom together.'
'There is no one on the ceiling; look for yourself.'
'What are they saying about you? Tell me everything.'
'Try to ignore them and they will go away.'
items.rationale: The therapeutic response presents reality by stating that the nurse does not share the perception, acknowledges the client's feelings, and redirects to a real activity, which reduces the hallucination's hold without arguing. Asking for full details reinforces the hallucination, pointing at the ceiling challenges and can agitate the client, and telling the client to ignore the voices dismisses a symptom the client cannot simply switch off.

items.stem: A client with antisocial personality disorder tells the nurse, 'The other nurse lets me smoke on the patio whenever I want; you're just being difficult.' Which response by the nurse is best?
options: 'You always try to bend the rules; why can't you follow them like everyone else?'
'The rule is one supervised smoke break at 1000 and 1500 for everyone, and that applies today.'
'Fine, just this once, but do not tell the others.'
'I will check with the other nurse and get back to you.'
items.rationale: Clients with antisocial personality disorder test limits and try to manipulate staff; the effective response is a calm, matter-of-fact restatement of the rule that applies to everyone, delivered consistently by all staff. Deferring to another nurse invites splitting, making an exception rewards manipulation and undermines the whole team, and a judgmental 'you always' statement is a power struggle that damages the relationship without setting a limit.

items.stem: A 27-year-old client is brought to the emergency department by family after 4 days without sleep; the client is talking rapidly about a plan to buy a hotel, has spent 12,000 dollars on jewelry, and has eaten only a few crackers in 2 days. Complete the diagram by selecting the condition the client is most likely experiencing, 2 actions the nurse should take, and 2 parameters the nurse should monitor to assess progress.
bowtieActions: Discharge home with instructions to sleep
Offer high-calorie finger foods and fluids frequently
Confront the client about the reckless spending
Provide a low-stimulus environment with a consistent staff member
Encourage participation in a competitive group game to burn off energy
bowtieParams: Food and fluid intake and weight
items.rationale: Days without sleep, pressured speech, grandiose plans and impulsive spending define acute mania; depression with psychosis would show low mood and energy, delirium would show fluctuating consciousness and inattention, and panic is episodic. Reducing stimulation and providing portable nutrition address the safety and physiological risks of mania, while sleep hours and intake with weight are the parameters that show whether the episode is settling. Competitive games and confrontation escalate the client, and discharge is unsafe.

items.stem: The nurse is caring for a client admitted with melena and reviews the data collected since arrival. Which conclusion should the nurse draw?
options: The tachycardia is caused by anxiety and should be treated with a benzodiazepine before rechecking labs
The falling hemoglobin reflects hemodilution from IV fluids and no change in the plan is needed
The bleeding has stopped because the hemoglobin is falling more slowly with each interval
The client has ongoing hemorrhage and requires immediate provider notification and preparation for transfusion
items.rationale: A steady fall in hemoglobin and hematocrit with progressive tachycardia, falling blood pressure and worsening orthostatic symptoms ending in syncope indicates active blood loss with failing compensation, so the provider is notified and blood products are prepared. Hemodilution would not produce escalating hypotension and syncope, the interval drops are not slowing, and treating the tachycardia as anxiety would mask a compensatory response to hypovolemia.

items.stem: A client with heart failure receives daily furosemide and digoxin. The nurse reviews the trended laboratory values. Which findings require follow-up with the provider? Select all that apply.
options: Magnesium of 2.0 mg/dL on day 1
Digoxin level of 2.3 ng/mL on day 4
Potassium of 2.9 mEq/L on day 4
Heart rate of 52 beats/min on day 4
Sodium of 136 mEq/L on day 4
Heart rate of 74 beats/min on day 2
items.rationale: Loop diuretics waste potassium and magnesium, and low levels of both sensitize the heart to digoxin; the digoxin level has climbed above the 2.0 ng/mL toxic threshold while the heart rate has fallen to 52, a classic early toxicity sign. The nurse holds the digoxin, reports the potassium, magnesium, level and bradycardia, and anticipates electrolyte replacement and an ECG. Sodium of 136 and the day 1 magnesium and day 2 heart rate are within expected limits.

items.stem: A client with type 2 diabetes underwent a CT scan with IV iodinated contrast on day 0. The nurse reviews the renal trend. Which conclusion should the nurse draw?
options: The values reflect expected diuresis after the fluid load given with the contrast
The client is developing contrast-induced acute kidney injury; the nurse should notify the provider and confirm that metformin remains on hold
The trend is stable because the creatinine remains under 3.0 mg/dL
The rising BUN indicates dehydration that will resolve with an oral fluid challenge alone
items.rationale: A creatinine rise of more than 0.3 mg/dL within 48-72 hours of contrast defines contrast-induced acute kidney injury; here it has more than doubled with falling eGFR and urine output. Metformin must stay held until kidney function returns to baseline because it accumulates and can cause lactic acidosis. Diuresis would raise, not lower, urine output, dehydration alone elevates BUN out of proportion to creatinine, and a sharply rising creatinine is not stable simply because it is under 3.0.

items.stem: A client was admitted after an acetaminophen overdose and is receiving IV acetylcysteine. The nurse reviews the trended values. Which conclusion should the nurse draw?
options: The rising INR is an expected effect of acetylcysteine and does not need to be reported
The bilirubin rise indicates hemolysis from the antidote rather than liver injury
The client is recovering because the transaminases have begun to fall at 84 hours
The client is progressing to acute liver failure with worsening synthetic function and encephalopathy; the nurse should escalate care immediately
items.rationale: Falling transaminases while INR and bilirubin keep rising and mental status deteriorates means hepatocytes are dying and can no longer release enzymes, not that the liver is healing. INR is the most sensitive marker of hepatic synthetic function, and its rise with encephalopathy meets criteria for acute liver failure requiring transplant-center evaluation. Acetylcysteine does not raise the INR meaningfully or cause hemolysis, so those explanations are false reassurance.

items.stem: A client has received a continuous heparin infusion since admission for a pulmonary embolism. Based on the trended data, which action should the nurse take first?
options: Increase the heparin rate because a new clot has formed despite therapy
Request a platelet transfusion to correct the platelet count
Stop the heparin infusion and all heparin flushes, then notify the provider
Continue the infusion because the aPTT has remained in the therapeutic range
trendRows: New swelling of the left calf
items.rationale: A platelet fall of more than 50% from baseline beginning 5-10 days into heparin therapy, accompanied by a new thrombosis, is the classic picture of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia, an immune reaction that causes clotting rather than bleeding. All heparin exposure, including line flushes, must stop at once, and the provider will order HIT antibody testing and a non-heparin anticoagulant. Platelet transfusion increases thrombosis risk, and a therapeutic aPTT does not exclude HIT.

items.stem: A client with diabetic ketoacidosis is receiving 0.9% sodium chloride and a regular insulin infusion. Based on the trend, which action should the nurse take first?
options: Stop the insulin infusion because the glucose is now near normal
Increase the insulin rate because the anion gap is still elevated
Hold potassium replacement because the potassium started above the normal range
Notify the provider that the glucose is below 250 mg/dL and the potassium is falling, and anticipate adding dextrose to the fluids and increasing potassium replacement
items.rationale: Insulin drives both glucose and potassium into cells, so serum potassium falls steadily during DKA treatment even when it started high; a level of 3.1 mEq/L with insulin still running risks a lethal dysrhythmia and needs more replacement. Once glucose reaches about 200-250 mg/dL, dextrose is added so insulin can continue to close the anion gap without causing hypoglycemia. Stopping insulin lets ketoacidosis rebound, and increasing it accelerates the fall in glucose and potassium.

items.stem: The nurse reviews the vital sign flowsheet of a client who is postoperative day 2 after a bowel resection. Which action should the nurse take first?
options: Administer the scheduled acetaminophen and reassess in 1 hour
Encourage oral fluids and document the findings
Activate the rapid response team and notify the surgeon
Apply oxygen at 2 L/min and continue hourly vital signs
items.rationale: Rising temperature, heart rate and respiratory rate with falling blood pressure and oxygen saturation and new confusion produce a high early-warning score that signals evolving septic shock after abdominal surgery. Immediate escalation brings the team needed for cultures, a 30 mL/kg crystalloid bolus and antibiotics within the hour. An antipyretic, low-flow oxygen or oral fluids alone treat a single number while the client continues to deteriorate.

items.stem: Click to highlight the findings in the preoperative laboratory report that the nurse should report to the surgical team before the client goes to the operating room.

highlightSegments.text: Preoperative labs, 0600, client scheduled for laparoscopic cholecystectomy at 0900.
Hemoglobin 13.8 g/dL, hematocrit 41%.
White blood cells 7.4 x 10^3/uL.
Platelets 232,000/mm3.
Potassium 3.0 mEq/L.
Sodium 140 mEq/L, creatinine 0.9 mg/dL.
Fasting glucose 246 mg/dL.
INR 1.9, with the medication list showing warfarin taken last evening.
Urinalysis negative for infection.
Client reports NPO since midnight.

items.rationale: A potassium of 3.0 mEq/L raises the risk of intraoperative dysrhythmias, a glucose above 200 mg/dL increases surgical site infection risk and needs control, and an INR of 1.9 with warfarin taken the night before means anticoagulation was not held as required, so surgical bleeding risk is high. The surgeon and anesthesia provider must decide whether to correct these or postpone. The CBC, sodium, creatinine, urinalysis and NPO status are within expected limits.

items.stem: Click to highlight the findings in the nurses' note that require immediate follow-up after a cardiac catheterization.

highlightSegments.text: 1400: Client returned from the catheterization lab; right femoral access with closure device in place.
Bed rest maintained with the right leg straight, head of bed at 30 degrees.
1415: Site dry, no hematoma; right pedal pulse 2+, foot warm, BP 128/76, HR 82.
1445: Client reports the right foot feels 'asleep' and cold.
Right pedal pulse now faint by Doppler only; left pedal pulse 2+.
1500: Firm 4 cm swelling palpated beneath the dressing at the puncture site, larger than at 1445.
Client drinking water as encouraged to clear the contrast.
Voided 300 mL of clear yellow urine.
Pain at the site rated 2/10.

items.rationale: A cold, numb foot with a pulse that has become Doppler-only indicates arterial occlusion or compression distal to the access site, and an enlarging firm swelling with falling blood pressure and rising heart rate indicates an expanding hematoma or retroperitoneal bleeding. Both are limb- and life-threatening, so the nurse applies pressure, notifies the provider and prepares for vascular intervention. Hydration, voiding, a straight leg and mild site pain are expected after catheterization.

items.stem: Click to highlight the findings in the post-procedure note that the nurse should report to the provider immediately.

highlightSegments.text: 1030: Thoracentesis completed at the bedside on the left; 1,300 mL of straw-colored fluid removed.
Puncture site dressing dry and intact.
1045: Client states, 'I can breathe so much better.'
RR 18, SpO2 96% on room air, breath sounds now present on the left.
1130: Client reports sudden shortness of breath and a persistent cough.
Coughing up frothy, pink-tinged sputum.
RR 30, SpO2 88% on room air, HR 118.
Trachea midline.
Fine crackles heard throughout the left lung field.
Client requests something to drink.

items.rationale: Sudden dyspnea, hypoxemia, cough with frothy pink sputum and new diffuse crackles within an hour of draining a large pleural effusion are the picture of re-expansion pulmonary edema, which can progress rapidly to respiratory failure; the nurse applies oxygen, sits the client upright and notifies the provider at once. A midline trachea makes tension pneumothorax unlikely. The dry dressing, immediate relief and initially normal vital signs are expected after thoracentesis.

items.stem: Click to highlight the findings in the home health note that require the nurse to contact the provider.

highlightSegments.text: Home visit, day 6 after a long-arm fiberglass cast was applied for a distal radius fracture.
Client reports pain 3/10 at rest, controlled with acetaminophen.
Fingers pink and warm, capillary refill 2 seconds.
Client able to wiggle all fingers.
A foul odor is noted at the wrist end of the cast,
and the cast feels warm over the palmar surface.
Client reports a 'burning' sensation under the cast that started yesterday.
Temperature 38.2 C (100.8 F) this morning.
Cast edges are padded with no skin breakdown at the edges.
Client keeps the arm elevated on pillows when sitting.

items.rationale: A foul odor, a localized hot spot on the cast, burning pain and a fever indicate infection or a pressure injury developing beneath the cast, which cannot be inspected without a cast window or removal, so the provider must be contacted. Circulation, sensation and movement are intact, so compartment syndrome is not suggested. Controlled pain, padded edges and elevation are appropriate findings for a healing fracture.

items.stem: Click to highlight the laboratory values that the nurse should report to the provider for a client on day 3 of total parenteral nutrition after 2 weeks of minimal oral intake.

highlightSegments.text: Day 3 TPN laboratory panel, drawn at 0500.
Glucose 296 mg/dL.
Sodium 141 mEq/L.
Potassium 3.1 mEq/L.
Chloride 102 mEq/L.
Phosphorus 1.3 mg/dL.
Magnesium 1.4 mg/dL.
Calcium 9.0 mg/dL.
BUN 16 mg/dL, creatinine 0.8 mg/dL.
Triglycerides 148 mg/dL.
ALT 28 units/L, AST 24 units/L.

items.rationale: After prolonged starvation, the carbohydrate load of TPN drives phosphorus, potassium and magnesium into cells; the resulting refeeding syndrome can cause respiratory failure, dysrhythmias and seizures, so these low values must be reported and replaced and the infusion rate reassessed. A glucose near 300 mg/dL also requires insulin adjustment or a slower rate. Sodium, chloride, calcium, renal function, triglycerides and transaminases are within normal limits.

items.stem: Complete the following sentences by choosing from the lists of options.
items.clozeText: A client who is 3 days postoperative from an open abdominal hysterectomy reports new aching in the left calf, which is warmer and 3 cm larger in circumference than the right. The nurse should first {{1}} and anticipate an order for {{2}}.

options: have the client dorsiflex the foot repeatedly to confirm the diagnosis
apply a warm compress and ambulate the client in the hall
massage the calf to relieve the cramp
keep the client in bed with the leg elevated and notify the provider
a chest x-ray
an ankle x-ray
a venous duplex ultrasound of the leg
a 12-lead electrocardiogram

items.rationale: Unilateral calf pain, warmth and swelling after pelvic surgery are cues for deep vein thrombosis; the client stays in bed with the limb elevated to reduce the chance of dislodging the clot while the provider is notified, and venous duplex ultrasound is the standard confirmatory test. Massage, ambulation and repeated dorsiflexion can dislodge a thrombus and are no longer recommended; x-rays and an ECG do not image venous clots.

items.stem: Complete the following sentences by choosing from the lists of options.
items.clozeText: Twenty minutes into a procedure under general anesthesia with succinylcholine and sevoflurane, the client develops masseter muscle rigidity, a heart rate of 138 beats/min and an end-tidal CO2 that has risen from 38 to 62 mm Hg. The circulating nurse recognizes {{1}}, the priority medication to prepare is {{2}}, and the team should also expect {{3}}.

options: a tension pneumothorax
malignant hyperthermia
anaphylaxis to the anesthetic
inadequate depth of anesthesia
dantrolene
epinephrine
succinylcholine
calcium gluconate
a rapid rise in core temperature and dark urine from myoglobinuria
hypotension that resolves after a fluid bolus
bronchospasm relieved by albuterol
a fall in end-tidal CO2 once the surgery is completed

items.rationale: A rising end-tidal CO2 with muscle rigidity and tachycardia after a volatile agent and succinylcholine is the earliest pattern of malignant hyperthermia, a hypermetabolic crisis of skeletal muscle; the temperature spike comes later, and muscle breakdown produces myoglobinuria. Dantrolene is the specific antidote and must be reconstituted immediately. Epinephrine treats anaphylaxis, which presents with hypotension and bronchospasm rather than rigidity and rising CO2.

items.stem: Complete the following sentences by choosing from the lists of options.
items.clozeText: On postoperative day 7 after abdominal surgery, a client with obesity coughs forcefully and says 'something just popped.' The nurse sees a loop of bowel protruding through the incision. The nurse should first {{1}}, position the client {{2}}, and {{3}}.

options: push the bowel gently back through the incision
paint the exposed bowel with povidone-iodine
cover the bowel with sterile gauze moistened with sterile normal saline
apply a dry pressure dressing and an abdominal binder
in high Fowler's position
on the right side with the legs straight
supine in low Fowler's position with the knees flexed
prone with a pillow under the abdomen
keep the client NPO and notify the surgeon immediately
encourage coughing to clear the airway
document the finding and reassess in 30 minutes
offer clear liquids to reduce anxiety

items.rationale: Evisceration is a surgical emergency: moist sterile saline gauze keeps the exposed bowel from drying while low Fowler's position with the knees flexed reduces tension on the abdominal wall, and the surgeon is notified because the client must return to the operating room, so nothing is given by mouth. The viscera are never pushed back or painted with antiseptic, dry dressings damage the bowel, and coughing or high Fowler's position increases intra-abdominal pressure.

items.stem: Complete the following sentences by choosing from the lists of options.
items.clozeText: The morning after a lumbar puncture, a client reports a throbbing headache that is severe when sitting up and almost gone when lying flat. The nurse recognizes this as {{1}} and should {{2}}; if the headache persists despite these measures, the nurse anticipates {{3}}.

options: increased intracranial pressure from a hematoma
early meningitis from the procedure
a migraine unrelated to the procedure
a post-dural puncture headache from cerebrospinal fluid leakage
place the client in high Fowler's position and restrict fluids
apply ice to the puncture site and ambulate the client
keep the client flat, encourage fluids, and give the prescribed analgesic and caffeine
perform neurologic checks every 15 minutes and prepare for a CT scan
a repeat lumbar puncture
IV antibiotics
an epidural blood patch
a lumbar drain

items.rationale: A positional headache that is worse upright and relieved when supine within 48 hours of dural puncture results from continued CSF leakage and low intracranial pressure; lying flat, hydration, analgesics and caffeine are first-line, and an epidural blood patch seals the leak when conservative care fails. Meningitis presents with fever and nuchal rigidity, and a hematoma or raised intracranial pressure causes headache with neurologic deficits that would not improve by lying down.

items.stem: Complete the following sentences by choosing from the lists of options.
items.clozeText: A client with chronic hepatitis is scheduled for a percutaneous liver biopsy. Before the procedure the nurse verifies the {{1}}. Afterward, the client is positioned {{2}} for several hours, and the nurse monitors most closely for {{3}}.

options: fasting blood glucose
prothrombin time, INR and platelet count
urine specific gravity
serum amylase and lipase
on the left side with the knees drawn up
supine with the legs elevated
prone with the head of the bed elevated 45 degrees
on the right side with a pillow pressed against the puncture site
hemorrhage, shown by tachycardia, hypotension and right shoulder pain
a headache that worsens when sitting up
hypoglycemia from fasting before the procedure
urinary retention from the sedative

items.rationale: The liver is highly vascular, so coagulation status determines whether the biopsy can safely proceed; lying on the right side compresses the puncture site against the chest wall to tamponade bleeding, and hemorrhage is the most serious complication, often signaled by referred right shoulder pain from diaphragmatic irritation along with tachycardia and hypotension. Pancreatic enzymes, glucose and specific gravity are not procedure-critical, and a positional headache follows lumbar puncture.

items.stem: Complete the following sentences by choosing from the lists of options.
items.clozeText: A client with cirrhosis and tense ascites is scheduled for a large-volume paracentesis. Immediately before the procedure the nurse should have the client {{1}}. After 5 liters are removed, the nurse monitors for {{2}} and anticipates administering {{3}}.

options: hold their breath during needle insertion
drink 500 mL of water
lie flat on the left side
empty the bladder
hypotension and tachycardia from fluid shifts
urinary retention from abdominal pressure
hypertension and bradycardia from vagal stimulation
hyperglycemia from stress
IV albumin
oral lactulose
IV furosemide
a unit of packed red blood cells

items.rationale: An empty bladder reduces the chance of puncturing it when the needle enters the lower abdomen. Removing more than 4-5 liters shifts fluid from the vascular space back into the peritoneum, causing hypovolemia, hypotension and renal hypoperfusion; IV albumin, usually 6-8 g per liter removed, restores oncotic pressure and prevents this circulatory dysfunction. A diuretic would worsen hypovolemia, blood is not indicated without hemorrhage, and lactulose treats encephalopathy.

items.stem: Complete the following sentences by choosing from the lists of options.
items.clozeText: Six hours after a closed tibial fracture was placed in a posterior splint and compression wrap, the client reports pain 10/10 that is unrelieved by IV morphine and worsens when the nurse passively moves the toes. The nurse suspects {{1}}, should first {{2}}, and should keep the limb {{3}}.

options: fat embolism syndrome
acute compartment syndrome
normal fracture pain requiring a higher opioid dose
a deep vein thrombosis
apply ice and elevate the leg above the heart
apply a warm compress to improve circulation
administer an additional dose of morphine and reassess in 30 minutes
loosen the compression wrap and splint and notify the provider immediately
wrapped tightly to reduce swelling
elevated above the heart on three pillows
at the level of the heart
dependent over the side of the bed

items.rationale: Pain out of proportion to the injury, unrelieved by opioids and increased by passive stretch, is the earliest and most reliable sign of compartment syndrome; pulses are lost late. Any constricting device is released immediately and the provider is notified for compartment pressure measurement and possible fasciotomy. Keeping the limb at heart level preserves arterial perfusion; elevation above the heart lowers perfusion pressure and ice causes vasoconstriction, so both worsen ischemia.

items.stem: The nurse assesses a client 2 hours after a colonoscopy with polypectomy performed under moderate sedation. For each finding, click to specify whether the finding is expected or requires follow-up.
matrixRows: Mild abdominal cramping relieved after passing flatus
Heart rate 118 beats/min with blood pressure 88/54 mm Hg
Drowsiness that resolves when the client is spoken to
Severe, steady abdominal pain with a rigid, board-like abdomen
A few streaks of blood on the tissue after the first bowel movement
Temperature 38.6 C (101.5 F) with chills
Passing large amounts of dark red blood and clots from the rectum
items.rationale: Air insufflated during the procedure causes cramping that resolves with flatus, residual sedation causes drowsiness that is easily roused, and minor streaking after polypectomy is common. Tachycardia with hypotension and passage of clots suggest hemorrhage from the polypectomy site, while severe pain with a rigid abdomen and fever with chills indicate perforation with peritonitis; each requires immediate provider notification.

items.stem: A client with an eGFR of 42 mL/min/1.73 m2 is scheduled for an MRI of the lumbar spine with gadolinium contrast. For each nursing action, click to specify whether it is indicated, contraindicated, or non-essential.
matrixRows: Screen the client for a pacemaker, cochlear implant, or retained metal fragments
Communicate the eGFR to the radiology team before the contrast is given
Remove a transdermal medication patch that has a metal-backed foil
Keep the client NPO for 12 hours before the scan
Leave the client's insulin pump in place during the scan
Ask about claustrophobia and offer the prescribed anxiolytic if ordered
items.rationale: The magnetic field can dislodge ferromagnetic objects, heat metal-backed patches and disable electronic devices, so implant screening, patch removal and removing an insulin pump are safety essentials. Reduced kidney function raises the risk of nephrogenic systemic fibrosis with gadolinium, so radiology must know the eGFR to choose the agent and dose. Prolonged fasting is not required for an MRI without sedation, and screening for claustrophobia improves scan completion.

items.stem: A client returns to the unit after a flexible bronchoscopy with transbronchial biopsy performed under moderate sedation with topical lidocaine to the throat. Which actions should the nurse take during the first hour? Select all that apply.
options: Encourage vigorous coughing to clear the anesthetic from the airway
Position the client in semi-Fowler's position
Offer warm tea to soothe the throat as soon as the client is awake
Keep the client NPO until the gag and swallow reflexes return
Assess for stridor, dyspnea, and diminished breath sounds on one side
Report small amounts of blood-tinged sputum immediately as hemorrhage
Monitor oxygen saturation continuously
items.rationale: Topical lidocaine numbs the pharynx, so oral intake waits until the gag and swallow reflexes return; semi-Fowler's position and continuous pulse oximetry support ventilation after sedation, and unilateral diminished breath sounds, stridor and dyspnea are signs of pneumothorax or laryngospasm after a transbronchial biopsy. Fluids before reflex return cause aspiration, vigorous coughing can restart bleeding at the biopsy site, and small amounts of blood-tinged sputum are expected after biopsy.

items.stem: The nurse is preparing a client for a cardiac catheterization with iodinated contrast. Which finding is the priority to report to the provider before the procedure?
options: The client took the prescribed metoprolol with a sip of water at 0600
Pedal pulses 2+ and equal bilaterally
Serum creatinine 2.4 mg/dL
Hemoglobin 12.9 g/dL
items.rationale: Iodinated contrast is nephrotoxic, and a creatinine of 2.4 mg/dL indicates existing kidney impairment that greatly raises the risk of contrast-induced acute kidney injury; the provider may order pre-hydration, a reduced contrast dose or a delay. A hemoglobin of 12.9 g/dL is normal, beta-blockers are usually continued with a sip of water on the morning of the procedure, and equal pedal pulses are the normal baseline needed for post-procedure comparison.

items.stem: A client is 36 hours after a closed femur fracture stabilized in skeletal traction. The client is restless and confused, RR 32, SpO2 87% on room air, temperature 38.6 C (101.5 F), with petechiae across the chest and axillae. Complete the diagram by selecting the condition the client is most likely experiencing, 2 actions the nurse should take, and 2 parameters the nurse should monitor to assess progress.
bowtieActions: Elevate the fractured leg above heart level and apply ice
Remove the traction weights to reduce pain
Apply high-flow oxygen and notify the provider immediately
Minimize movement of the fractured extremity
Encourage the client to ambulate to the chair
bowtieParams: Pain with passive stretch of the toes
items.rationale: Confusion, hypoxemia, tachypnea, fever and a petechial rash 24-72 hours after a long-bone fracture form the classic triad of fat embolism syndrome. Care is supportive: high-flow oxygen with early escalation, and keeping the fracture immobilized to stop further marrow fat release. Effectiveness is judged by improving saturation, respiratory rate and mentation. Compartment syndrome causes pain on passive stretch, DVT changes calf size, and neither explains petechiae or confusion.

items.stem: A client receiving hydromorphone by patient-controlled analgesia after a spinal fusion has the following trended data. Which action should the nurse take first?
options: Stop the PCA, stimulate the client, support ventilation with oxygen, and prepare to give naloxone
Apply oxygen at 2 L/min by nasal cannula and recheck the saturation in 30 minutes
Administer sodium bicarbonate to correct the acidosis
Reduce the PCA demand dose by half and continue hourly checks
items.rationale: A falling respiratory rate, a rising sedation score and a PaCO2 climbing to 62 mm Hg with a pH of 7.25 show acute respiratory acidosis from opioid-induced hypoventilation; the nearly unchanged bicarbonate confirms it is acute. The opioid is stopped, the client is roused and ventilated, and naloxone reverses the depression. Oxygen alone can normalize the pulse oximeter while carbon dioxide keeps rising, halving the dose is too slow, and bicarbonate does not correct a ventilation problem.

items.stem: A client with urosepsis received a 30 mL/kg crystalloid bolus and IV antibiotics on arrival to the emergency department. The nurse reviews the data trend. Which conclusion should the nurse draw?
options: The client is developing fluid overload because the urine output has increased
The resuscitation is effective and the current plan should continue with ongoing reassessment
The lactate should be rechecked only if it begins to rise again
The client needs a vasopressor because the mean arterial pressure has not exceeded 80 mm Hg
items.rationale: Lactate clearance to below 2 mmol/L, a mean arterial pressure sustained above 65 mm Hg, a falling heart rate, urine output above 0.5 mL/kg/hr and return of clear mentation are the standard markers of restored tissue perfusion after sepsis resuscitation. Vasopressors are indicated when the MAP stays below 65 despite fluids, not to push it above 80. Rising urine output reflects restored renal perfusion rather than overload, and lactate is rechecked on schedule.

items.stem: A client presented to the emergency department with 2 hours of chest pressure. The nurse reviews the serial results. Which conclusion should the nurse draw?
options: The rising troponin pattern confirms acute myocardial injury, and the provider must be notified immediately even though the pain is easing
The falling pain score shows the myocardial injury has resolved
Because there is no ST elevation, the client is not having a myocardial infarction
The initial normal troponin rules out a cardiac cause, and the client can be discharged after the 6-hour value
trendRows: New T-wave inversion in leads II, III, aVF
T-wave inversion persists, no ST elevation
items.rationale: Troponin is the most specific marker of myocardial necrosis; a value that climbs to more than 40 times the upper reference limit across serial draws, with new dynamic T-wave changes in the inferior leads, is diagnostic of an evolving non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction. A single early troponin can be normal because the marker takes 3-6 hours to rise, and absence of ST elevation defines NSTEMI rather than excluding infarction. Easing pain does not mean the injury has stopped.

items.stem: A client is 2 days postoperative after a bowel resection and has received dextrose 5% in water at 125 mL/hr since surgery. The nurse reviews the trend. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.
options: Perform neurologic checks at least hourly
Administer the prescribed docusate and document the findings
Initiate seizure precautions
Stop the dextrose 5% infusion and notify the provider immediately
Encourage the client to drink additional water to increase urine output
Prepare to give 3% sodium chloride as a rapid 1-liter bolus
items.rationale: Falling sodium and osmolality with weight gain and decreasing urine output on a hypotonic infusion indicate dilutional hyponatremia, likely worsened by postoperative antidiuretic hormone release; at 118 mEq/L with confusion and twitching, seizures are imminent. Free water must stop, seizure precautions and frequent neurologic checks begin, and the provider will order cautious hypertonic saline in small doses because rapid correction causes osmotic demyelination. Extra water and routine care worsen the situation.

items.stem: A nurse in a primary care clinic reviews the record of a client with type 2 diabetes who takes metformin and reports 'feeling fine.' Which conclusion should the nurse draw from the trend?
options: Glycemic control is worsening and early nephropathy and neuropathy are emerging, so the nurse should explore barriers and anticipate intensified treatment
The A1c reflects only the past week, so a single high-carbohydrate meal explains the change
The weight gain shows improved nutrition and offsets the rise in A1c
Because the client feels well, the current regimen is adequate and follow-up can be extended to yearly
items.rationale: A1c reflects average glucose over about 3 months; a steady climb from 6.7% to 9.3% with rising fasting glucose shows the regimen is no longer effective, and an albumin-to-creatinine ratio above 30 mg/g plus loss of vibration sense are early microvascular complications. Feeling well is typical of chronic hyperglycemia, and weight gain worsens insulin resistance. The nurse assesses adherence, diet and access to care and expects the provider to add therapy and shorten follow-up.

items.stem: The nurse monitors a client 8 hours after coronary artery bypass grafting. Based on the trended data, which conclusion should the nurse draw?
options: The abrupt stop in drainage with rising CVP, narrowing pulse pressure and muffled heart sounds indicates cardiac tamponade; the surgeon must be notified immediately
The client is hypovolemic from earlier blood loss and needs only a fluid bolus
The rising CVP indicates fluid overload and a diuretic should be requested
The decreasing drainage shows the bleeding has stopped and the chest tube can be clamped
items.rationale: Drainage that falls from 140 mL/hr to zero while the client deteriorates means blood is collecting in the pericardium instead of draining; a clotted mediastinal tube after cardiac surgery is a classic cause of tamponade. Rising CVP, a narrowing pulse pressure of 84/72, tachycardia and muffled heart sounds complete the picture, and emergency drainage or re-exploration is needed. Hypovolemia would lower the CVP, a diuretic would worsen output, and clamping the tube accelerates tamponade.

items.stem: The nurse reviews the postoperative course of a client who had an open colectomy. Based on the trend, which action should the nurse take first?
options: Hold all oral intake and notify the surgeon; anticipate a nasogastric tube to low intermittent suction
Administer the prescribed prochlorperazine and continue clear liquids
Advance the diet to full liquids to stimulate peristalsis
Encourage ambulation and document the findings as expected on postoperative day 4
items.rationale: Absent bowel sounds, a girth increasing by 12 cm, no flatus and escalating bilious vomiting on day 4 indicate a prolonged paralytic ileus or early obstruction with gut distention that risks aspiration and electrolyte loss; the bowel is rested and decompressed with a nasogastric tube while the surgeon evaluates. Feeding a non-functioning bowel worsens distention, an antiemetic treats only the symptom, and ambulation helps prevent ileus but cannot resolve this degree of distention.

items.stem: Click to highlight the findings in the telemetry flowsheet that the nurse should report to the provider.

highlightSegments.text: Telemetry flowsheet, night shift, client admitted yesterday with an inferior wall myocardial infarction.
2300: Sinus rhythm 72/min, PR 0.18 s, QRS 0.08 s, QTc 440 ms.
0100: Sinus rhythm 76/min with 2 unifocal PVCs per minute; client asleep.
0300: Multifocal PVCs increasing to 10 per minute.
0310: Six-beat run of ventricular tachycardia, self-terminated; client denies symptoms.
0400: Repeat labs show potassium 3.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.5 mg/dL.
Hemoglobin 13.1 g/dL, troponin trending down.
0500: Sinus rhythm 70/min, QTc now 528 ms after an antiemetic was given at 0430.
Client resting comfortably, chest pain 0/10.
Capillary glucose 132 mg/dL.

items.rationale: Increasing multifocal PVCs and a run of ventricular tachycardia after a myocardial infarction are warning arrhythmias for ventricular fibrillation, and they are being fueled by hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia that must be replaced; a QTc above 500 ms after a QT-prolonging antiemetic raises the risk of torsades de pointes and requires review of that medication. Occasional unifocal PVCs, normal intervals, a falling troponin, stable hemoglobin and a normal glucose are expected findings.

items.stem: Click to highlight the findings in the post-procedure note that indicate the client is developing a complication after a percutaneous liver biopsy.

highlightSegments.text: 1300: Percutaneous liver biopsy completed; client placed on the right side with a pillow against the site.
1315: BP 124/78, HR 82, site dressing dry.
1345: BP 118/74, HR 90; client reports mild soreness at the site.
1415: BP 102/66, HR 108; client reports new pain in the right shoulder.
Skin cool and pale; site dressing remains dry.
Abdomen firm and increasingly distended, tender to light touch in the right upper quadrant.
Client remains in the right side-lying position.
Repeat hemoglobin ordered.

items.rationale: A dry dressing does not exclude bleeding after liver biopsy because hemorrhage occurs into the peritoneum; falling blood pressure, rising heart rate, cool pale skin, referred right shoulder pain from diaphragmatic irritation and a firm, distending abdomen together indicate intra-abdominal hemorrhage requiring immediate provider notification, large-bore IV access and preparation for transfusion or intervention. Mild site soreness, stable early vital signs and correct positioning are expected.

items.stem: Click to highlight the findings in the home health note that require immediate follow-up by the nurse.

highlightSegments.text: Home visit for a client with end-stage kidney disease who has a left forearm arteriovenous fistula created 8 weeks ago.
Client reports dialysis three times weekly with no missed sessions.
The home health aide reports checking blood pressure on the left arm this morning because the right arm 'was sore.'
On palpation, the thrill over the fistula is absent,
and no bruit is heard with the stethoscope.
Left hand is cool with capillary refill of 4 seconds; client reports numb fingertips.
Skin over the fistula is intact without redness or drainage.
Client demonstrates correct hand-washing technique.
Weight is 1 kg above the last post-dialysis weight.

items.rationale: A fistula that has lost its thrill and bruit has most likely thrombosed and needs urgent evaluation to salvage the access; a cool, numb hand with delayed capillary refill suggests steal syndrome, in which the fistula diverts blood from the hand, and also needs vascular review. Compressing the arm with a blood pressure cuff can cause clotting, so the aide's action must be corrected and reported. Intact skin, adherence, hand hygiene and a 1 kg interdialytic gain are acceptable.

items.stem: Click to highlight the parts of the preoperative history that the nurse must report to the anesthesia provider before surgery.

highlightSegments.text: Preoperative interview, client scheduled for a total hip arthroplasty under general anesthesia.
Client reports NPO since midnight.
States, 'My brother died during a hernia surgery years ago; they said his temperature shot up and his muscles went stiff.'
Allergies: penicillin (rash).
Home medications include lisinopril, taken this morning as instructed.
Client also takes aspirin 325 mg daily and 'took it with breakfast yesterday.'
Client uses a ginkgo biloba supplement daily and 'didn't think it counted as a medicine.'
Denies smoking; drinks one glass of wine on weekends.
Dentures in place, to be removed before transport.

items.rationale: A first-degree relative who developed high fever and muscle rigidity during anesthesia suggests familial malignant hyperthermia, so the anesthesia provider must avoid triggering agents and have dantrolene ready. Aspirin taken within the past few days and ginkgo both impair platelet function and raise surgical and neuraxial bleeding risk. NPO status, a documented allergy, a continued antihypertensive, moderate alcohol use and planned denture removal are expected elements of the history.

items.stem: Click to highlight the findings in the postoperative day 2 flowsheet that indicate the client is developing a pulmonary complication.

highlightSegments.text: Postoperative day 2, open cholecystectomy; client received oxycodone at 0600 for pain rated 6/10.
0800: Temperature 38.3 C (100.9 F),
HR 96, RR 24 and shallow,
SpO2 91% on room air, down from 96% yesterday.
Breath sounds diminished in both bases with fine crackles that partially clear with coughing.
Incision dry, edges approximated, no erythema.
Client has used the incentive spirometer twice since surgery 'because it hurts.'
Tolerating clear liquids; abdomen soft with hypoactive bowel sounds.
Voiding adequate amounts.

items.rationale: Low-grade fever within the first 48 hours, shallow tachypnea, falling saturation and diminished basilar breath sounds with crackles that clear with coughing are the classic presentation of atelectasis, and minimal incentive spirometer use because of pain is the cause; the nurse controls pain, then enforces deep breathing, spirometry and ambulation. A clean incision, tolerated liquids, hypoactive bowel sounds on day 2 and adequate voiding are expected.

items.stem: Complete the following sentences by choosing from the lists of options.
items.clozeText: A client with type 2 diabetes who takes metformin is scheduled for an abdominal CT with IV iodinated contrast. Before the scan the nurse verifies the {{1}}, and after the scan the nurse teaches the client to {{2}} to reduce the risk of {{3}}.

options: serum creatinine and eGFR
hemoglobin A1c
serum potassium
urine culture result
take an oral diuretic to flush out the contrast
take a double dose of metformin with the next meal to prevent hyperglycemia
restrict fluids for 24 hours to prevent contrast leakage
drink extra fluids and hold metformin for 48 hours until kidney function is rechecked
a delayed allergic reaction
hyperglycemia from the contrast dye
contrast-induced kidney injury and metformin-associated lactic acidosis
fluid overload and pulmonary edema

items.rationale: Iodinated contrast can reduce renal perfusion and injure tubules, so baseline kidney function is needed, and hydration is the best-established protective measure; metformin is held for 48 hours because if the kidneys are injured the drug accumulates and can cause lactic acidosis. Doubling metformin, restricting fluids or adding a diuretic each increases the risk of harm, and contrast does not raise blood glucose.

items.stem: Complete the following sentences by choosing from the lists of options.
items.clozeText: A client receiving a weight-based heparin infusion for a deep vein thrombosis has an aPTT of 112 seconds (goal 60-80 seconds) with no signs of bleeding. Following the standard nomogram, the nurse should {{1}}, and the reversal agent the nurse ensures is available is {{2}}.

options: increase the rate because the therapeutic goal has been exceeded only slightly
give a heparin bolus and continue the current rate
hold the infusion for 1 hour, restart at a reduced rate, and recheck the aPTT in 6 hours
discontinue the heparin permanently and start warfarin
tranexamic acid
protamine sulfate
vitamin K
idarucizumab

items.rationale: An aPTT well above the therapeutic range indicates excessive anticoagulation and bleeding risk; nomograms direct the nurse to hold briefly, reduce the rate and recheck in about 6 hours so the level settles into range. Protamine sulfate neutralizes heparin, whereas vitamin K reverses warfarin and idarucizumab reverses dabigatran. Increasing the rate or giving a bolus raises bleeding risk, and stopping heparin entirely leaves the clot untreated because warfarin takes days to become effective.

items.stem: Complete the following sentences by choosing from the lists of options.
items.clozeText: A client with type 1 diabetes on a medical unit is shaky and diaphoretic with a capillary glucose of 54 mg/dL and is able to swallow safely. The nurse should first give {{1}}, recheck the glucose in {{2}}, and once it is above 70 mg/dL, {{3}}.

options: IM glucagon
a peanut butter sandwich
the scheduled mealtime insulin
15 g of fast-acting carbohydrate such as 120 mL of juice
1 hour
5 minutes
30 minutes
15 minutes
withhold food for 2 hours to avoid rebound hyperglycemia
provide a snack with protein and complex carbohydrate if the next meal is more than an hour away
administer the correction insulin dose
give a second 15 g of carbohydrate regardless of the result

items.rationale: The rule of 15 treats hypoglycemia in a conscious client with 15 g of fast-acting carbohydrate, a recheck in 15 minutes and repeat treatment until the glucose exceeds 70 mg/dL, followed by a longer-acting snack to prevent recurrence. Glucagon is reserved for clients who cannot swallow safely, fat and protein slow absorption of the initial treatment, and giving insulin would deepen the hypoglycemia.

items.stem: Complete the following sentences by choosing from the lists of options.
items.clozeText: A client with acute kidney injury has a new tunneled dialysis catheter in the right internal jugular vein. The nurse should {{1}}, and after each dialysis session should assess for {{2}}. Fever with rigors that begins during a session most likely indicates {{3}}.

options: remove the dressing daily to inspect the exit site
use the catheter only for dialysis unless the nephrologist authorizes other use
use the catheter for all blood draws to spare peripheral veins
flush both lumens with normal saline every 4 hours
a bounding pulse and jugular venous distention
hypotension, dizziness and bleeding at the exit site
hyperglycemia
hypertension and bradycardia
a catheter-related bloodstream infection
dialysis disequilibrium syndrome
a transfusion reaction
an air embolism

items.rationale: Dialysis catheter lumens are filled with concentrated heparin or citrate locks and are reserved for dialysis; routine access raises infection and clotting risk and could flush the locked anticoagulant into the client. Fluid removal during dialysis commonly causes hypotension and dizziness, and the heparin used in the circuit increases exit-site bleeding. Rigors and fever during a session signal a catheter-related bloodstream infection that requires blood cultures and prompt antibiotics.

items.stem: Complete the following sentences by choosing from the lists of options.
items.clozeText: A client is in balanced skeletal traction with 7 kg of weight after a femoral shaft fracture. The nurse verifies that the weights {{1}} and recognizes that {{2}} at a pin site requires provider notification. To reduce the risk of complications from immobility, the nurse should {{3}}.

options: hang freely without touching the floor or bed frame
are removed during pin site care
are reduced when the client reports pain
rest on the floor whenever the client is repositioned
purulent drainage with spreading redness and increasing pain
dry crusting around the pin
mild tenderness on the first day
a small amount of clear serous drainage
teach deep breathing, ankle pumps of the unaffected leg, and use of the overhead trapeze
keep the client flat and discourage movement to protect the traction
remove the antiembolism stocking from the affected leg only at night
limit fluids to reduce the need for the bedpan

items.rationale: Traction must be continuous with the weights hanging free; weights that touch the floor or are lifted lose the corrective pull and can cause muscle spasm and malalignment. Serous drainage and crusting are normal at pin sites, but purulence, spreading erythema and increasing pain signal infection that can extend into the bone. Immobility raises the risk of atelectasis, thrombosis and pressure injury, so breathing exercises, movement of unaffected limbs and trapeze use are essential.

items.stem: Complete the following sentences by choosing from the lists of options.
items.clozeText: A 7-year-old child is 6 hours post-tonsillectomy. The nurse notes the child is swallowing frequently while dozing, and the pulse has risen from 92 to 128 beats/min. The nurse recognizes possible {{1}}, should {{2}}, and should keep the child {{3}}.

options: early dehydration
normal throat discomfort
hemorrhage from the surgical site
laryngospasm
inspect the throat with a light for trickling blood and notify the surgeon immediately
offer a red popsicle to soothe the throat
encourage the child to cough and clear the throat
give the scheduled acetaminophen and reassess in an hour
supine with the head flat
in high Fowler's position drinking ice water
gargling with warm saline
NPO and positioned on the side to allow drainage

items.rationale: Frequent swallowing in a drowsy child with a rising pulse is the earliest sign of post-tonsillectomy bleeding, because children swallow blood rather than spit it out; direct inspection and immediate surgeon notification are required because the child may need to return to the operating room. Red-colored fluids mimic blood, coughing and gargling disturb the clot, and waiting an hour risks hemorrhagic shock; side-lying prevents aspiration and NPO status prepares for possible surgery.

items.stem: Complete the following sentences by choosing from the lists of options.
items.clozeText: During a telehealth call the day before a screening colonoscopy, a client who takes clopidogrel asks what to do about the medication and how to know whether the bowel prep is working. The nurse should {{1}}, instruct the client to avoid {{2}} during the clear-liquid diet, and explain that the prep is adequate when the stool becomes {{3}}.

options: state that clopidogrel has no effect on the procedure
advise the client to take a double dose of clopidogrel after the procedure
confirm that the prescriber has given specific instructions about holding or continuing clopidogrel
tell the client to stop the clopidogrel immediately until after the procedure
chicken broth
red or purple liquids and gelatin
clear apple juice
black coffee without cream
liquid with small brown flecks
clear or pale yellow liquid without solid particles
soft, brown and formed
dark and tarry

items.rationale: Antiplatelet decisions before a possible polypectomy balance bleeding against stent thrombosis and belong to the prescribing provider and endoscopist, so the nurse verifies the instruction rather than telling the client to stop. Red and purple dyes can be mistaken for blood in the colon, while clear juices, black coffee and broth are permitted clear liquids. Effluent that is clear or pale yellow means the colon is clean; particles or brown stool mean the prep is incomplete.

items.stem: A nurse reviews the pre-dialysis laboratory results of a client with end-stage kidney disease who receives hemodialysis three times weekly. For each result, click to specify whether it requires immediate reporting or is expected for this client before dialysis.
matrixRows: Potassium 6.4 mEq/L
BUN 64 mg/dL
Creatinine 8.2 mg/dL
Hemoglobin 6.9 g/dL, down from 10.4 g/dL last week
Phosphorus 5.8 mg/dL
Bicarbonate 20 mEq/L
matrixColumns: Expected before dialysis for this client
items.rationale: A potassium above 6 mEq/L can cause cardiac arrest and needs ECG monitoring and possibly emergent treatment before dialysis starts; a hemoglobin that has fallen 3.5 g/dL in a week signals bleeding rather than the stable anemia of kidney disease and requires investigation. Elevated BUN and creatinine, mild hyperphosphatemia and mild metabolic acidosis are the expected pre-dialysis picture in end-stage kidney disease and are corrected by the treatment and by phosphate binders.

items.stem: The nurse is reviewing findings documented for clients on a surgical unit. For each finding, click to specify the complication it most likely indicates.
matrixRows: Temperature 38.1 C (100.6 F) on postoperative day 1 with diminished breath sounds in the bases
Unilateral calf tenderness with 2 cm greater circumference on postoperative day 4
Purulent drainage and spreading erythema at the incision on postoperative day 5
Absent bowel sounds, abdominal distention and bilious vomiting on postoperative day 3
Oxygen saturation of 92% that improves to 96% after incentive spirometry
Temperature 38.7 C (101.7 F) on postoperative day 6 with the incision warm and tender
items.rationale: Timing helps sort postoperative complications: atelectasis appears within the first 48 hours and improves with lung expansion, deep vein thrombosis typically arises around days 3-7 with unilateral leg findings, wound infection declares itself after day 4-5 with local purulence, warmth and fever, and ileus presents as absent peristalsis with distention and vomiting once oral intake begins. Matching each finding to its usual window guides assessment and provider notification.

items.stem: The nurse is caring for a client with a chest tube connected to a wet-suction drainage system after a lobectomy. Which findings should the nurse report to the provider immediately? Select all that apply.
options: Sudden stop in drainage with new tachypnea and tracheal shift away from the affected side
Bright red drainage of 180 mL in the past hour
Crepitus spreading from the insertion site up the neck and face
Continuous bubbling in the water-seal chamber that was absent at the previous check
Water level in the water-seal chamber rising and falling with respirations
Pain of 3/10 at the insertion site with deep breathing
Gentle continuous bubbling in the suction control chamber
items.rationale: Bright drainage over 100 mL/hr suggests hemorrhage; new continuous water-seal bubbling indicates an air leak in the lung or the system; rapidly spreading subcutaneous emphysema means air is escaping into the tissue; and cessation of drainage with tracheal deviation signals a tension pneumothorax from a blocked tube. Gentle bubbling in the suction chamber and tidaling in the water seal show the system is working, and mild pain with deep breathing is expected.

items.stem: A client had a lumbar puncture 4 hours ago. Which findings should the nurse report to the provider? Select all that apply.
options: Clear fluid continuously leaking from the puncture site
New weakness and numbness in both legs
Temperature 38.8 C (101.8 F) with neck stiffness
Headache that is relieved when the client lies flat
Bruising the size of a coin at the needle site
Inability to void with a distended bladder on palpation
Mild aching at the puncture site rated 2/10
items.rationale: Bilateral leg weakness or numbness and new urinary retention suggest a spinal hematoma or nerve root compression, which can cause permanent deficit without urgent imaging and decompression; fever with nuchal rigidity suggests meningitis introduced by the procedure, and persistent leakage of cerebrospinal fluid prolongs low-pressure headache and creates an infection route. A positional headache treated with recumbency and fluids, mild site aching and a small bruise are expected.

items.stem: The charge nurse reviews the 0600 vital signs of four clients on a medical-surgical unit. Which client should the nurse assess first?
options: A client with pneumonia with HR 94 beats/min, RR 20 breaths/min, BP 132/80 mm Hg, temperature 38.1 C (100.6 F), and SpO2 94% on 2 L/min
A client with cellulitis with HR 88 beats/min, RR 18 breaths/min, BP 118/72 mm Hg, temperature 37.9 C (100.2 F), and SpO2 97% on room air
A client 1 day after a hip replacement with HR 118 beats/min, RR 26 breaths/min, BP 92/54 mm Hg, temperature 38.4 C (101.1 F), and new confusion
A client with a fractured ankle with HR 72 beats/min, RR 16 breaths/min, BP 152/90 mm Hg, and pain rated 7/10
items.rationale: Early warning tools assign points for each abnormal vital sign; tachycardia, tachypnea, hypotension, fever and an acute change in mental status together produce a high aggregate score that signals sepsis or shock and mandates immediate assessment and rapid response activation. The client with pneumonia has mild abnormalities on stable oxygen, an elevated blood pressure with pain is expected, and a low-grade temperature with otherwise normal vital signs scores low.

items.stem: Click to highlight the findings in the radiology nurse's note that indicate the client is having a reaction to the IV contrast that requires immediate action.

highlightSegments.text: 1010: IV iodinated contrast 100 mL injected for a CT of the chest through the right antecubital IV.
Client reports a warm flushing sensation spreading over the body and a metallic taste.
1013: Client states, 'My throat feels tight and I'm itchy all over.'
Raised hives noted on the chest and neck.
1015: Audible wheezing on expiration, RR 28.
BP 88/50, HR 122, down from 132/78 and 84 before the injection.
IV site without swelling or redness.
Client had mild nausea after contrast 2 years ago, documented on the screening form.
Scan completed; images being processed.

items.rationale: Throat tightness, urticaria, wheezing and hypotension with tachycardia within minutes of contrast are an anaphylactoid reaction that requires immediate epinephrine, oxygen, IV fluids and activation of the emergency response. Transient warmth and a metallic taste are expected physiologic effects of contrast, an intact IV site rules out extravasation, and prior mild nausea is a minor reaction that does not by itself require action now.

items.stem: Click to highlight the entries in the blood glucose flowsheet and nursing note that require follow-up with the provider.

highlightSegments.text: Client with type 2 diabetes prescribed NPH insulin 30 units at 2130 and 10 units at 0730.
2100: Glucose 168 mg/dL; evening NPH given as prescribed.
Client ate about one-quarter of the evening meal because of nausea.
0300: Glucose 46 mg/dL; client diaphoretic and difficult to wake.
Treated with dextrose 50% 25 mL IV per protocol; repeat glucose 118 mg/dL at 0320.
0700: Glucose 242 mg/dL; client reports a headache.
0730: Morning NPH dose is due.
Breakfast tray delivered; client eating 100%.
Vital signs stable throughout the shift.

items.rationale: Severe nocturnal hypoglycemia after a largely uneaten meal shows the fixed NPH dose exceeded the client's intake; the provider must review the regimen before the morning dose is given, and the 0700 value of 242 mg/dL may be rebound from counterregulatory hormones and the dextrose rather than a reason for more insulin. The evening dose given as prescribed, the protocol treatment, a full breakfast and stable vital signs are documentation, not new problems.

items.stem: Click to highlight the findings in the PACU handoff that indicate the client may be bleeding after a laparoscopic nephrectomy.

highlightSegments.text: 1530: Client arrived in the PACU after a left laparoscopic nephrectomy; estimated blood loss in the OR 150 mL.
1545: BP 122/76, HR 84, SpO2 98% on 2 L nasal cannula, alert.
Jackson-Pratt drain has filled with 160 mL of bright red output since arrival.
Client reports left flank pain 4/10, treated with fentanyl 25 mcg IV.
1645: BP 90/58, HR 122; client restless and asking for water repeatedly.
Skin cool and diaphoretic; capillary refill 4 seconds.
Urine output 15 mL over the past hour through the indwelling catheter.
Abdominal dressings dry; port sites intact.

items.rationale: Bright red drain output of 160 mL within an hour, progressive hypotension and tachycardia, restlessness with thirst, cool diaphoretic skin, delayed capillary refill and oliguria are the compensatory and then decompensating signs of hemorrhagic shock; dry dressings do not exclude internal bleeding after laparoscopic surgery. The surgeon is notified immediately for labs, fluids, blood products and possible return to the operating room. Moderate incisional pain and stable initial vital signs are expected.

items.stem: Click to highlight the findings in the dialysis flowsheet that require the nurse to intervene.

highlightSegments.text: Hemodialysis session 2 of 3 this week; target fluid removal 3.2 kg over 4 hours through the left arm fistula.
0800: BP 148/86, HR 78; client alert and reading.
0900: BP 132/80, HR 82; 1.1 kg removed.
1000: BP 96/58, HR 110; client reports feeling 'washed out' and nauseated.
Cramping in both calves reported.
1030: Client reports a headache and is having trouble following the conversation.
Fistula needles secure; blood flow rate 400 mL/min.
1100: Client vomited once; BP 88/52.
Dialysate temperature 36.5 C (97.7 F).

items.rationale: A rapid fall in blood pressure with nausea, cramping and vomiting is intradialytic hypotension from removing fluid faster than the vascular space can refill; the nurse slows or stops ultrafiltration, gives a saline bolus and lowers the head of the chair. A new headache with confusion during the session raises concern for disequilibrium syndrome from a rapid osmolar shift and requires a lower blood flow rate and provider notification. Stable early vital signs, secure needles and a normal dialysate temperature need no action.

items.stem: Click to highlight the findings in the anticoagulation clinic note that the nurse should report to the provider before the client leaves.

highlightSegments.text: Anticoagulation clinic visit; client takes warfarin 5 mg daily for atrial fibrillation, target INR 2.0-3.0.
INR today 5.6, up from 2.4 four weeks ago.
Client started a 10-day course of trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for a urinary tract infection 5 days ago.
Reports that urine has been 'pink' for 2 days.
Blood pressure 128/78, heart rate 76 and irregular.
Hemoglobin 11.2 g/dL, down from 13.6 g/dL at the last visit.
Client denies falls or head injury.
Reports eating a large green salad most days, unchanged from usual.
Asks whether the antibiotic should be finished.

items.rationale: An INR of 5.6 with hematuria and a 2.4 g/dL fall in hemoglobin indicates over-anticoagulation with active bleeding, and the recently started sulfonamide antibiotic inhibits warfarin metabolism and explains the rise; the provider will hold warfarin, consider vitamin K, evaluate the bleeding and address the interaction. Stable vital signs, an irregular pulse expected in atrial fibrillation, no head injury and unchanged vitamin K intake are context rather than new risks.

items.stem: Click to highlight the findings in the nurses' note that require immediate follow-up for a client 12 hours after a transurethral resection of the prostate with continuous bladder irrigation.

highlightSegments.text: 0200: Three-way catheter with continuous bladder irrigation infusing; return flow light pink.
Client reports bladder spasms relieved by the prescribed belladonna and opium suppository.
0400: Return flow now bright red with several clots,
and outflow has slowed despite increasing the irrigation rate.
Lower abdomen firm and distended; client reports severe suprapubic pressure.
0430: Client is nauseated and newly confused about where they are.
Serum sodium drawn at 0400 is pending.
Catheter secured to the thigh with traction maintained as ordered.

items.rationale: Bright red return with clots and slowing outflow with a distended bladder indicate hemorrhage and catheter obstruction that can rupture the bladder or dislodge the surgical clot; irrigation is stopped, the catheter may need manual irrigation per order, and the surgeon is notified.
